title: The Chrism Mass
hook: the bishop blesses the oils for the whole year's sacraments

segments.voice: Yesterday, Palm Sunday: hosanna at the door, crucify in the Passion. Your line was hosanna, then crucify.

In a Catholic parish church, often near the font or in a small cabinet in the wall called an ambry, there are three little vessels of oil. Every baby baptized there this year, every teenager confirmed, every elderly person anointed in a hospital bed, will be touched with oil from those vessels. And all of it came from one Mass, in one cathedral, during Holy Week, when the bishop and the priests of the diocese gathered in the same place.
screen: `THREE SMALL VESSELS.` → `EVERY BAPTISM, EVERY ANOINTING.` → `ONE MASS, ONE CATHEDRAL.`

segments.voice: It's called the Chrism Mass, traditionally celebrated on the morning of Holy Thursday, though some dioceses hold it earlier in Holy Week so priests from far-off parishes can come. Jars of olive oil are carried up the aisle, and the bishop blesses three. The oil of catechumens, for people preparing for baptism: a sign of strength for the struggle ahead. The oil of the sick, for the anointing of the sick. The letter of James describes it: "Is any man sick among you? Let him bring in the priests of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord." And the third, the sacred chrism. It's olive oil mixed with balsam, a fragrant resin, so it smells sweet. The bishop consecrates it, and by an old custom he breathes over it, a sign of the Spirit. Chrism is used at baptism, at confirmation, at the ordination of priests and bishops, and to consecrate altars and churches. Christ is a Greek title meaning anointed one; John's Gospel says so outright, that Messias, being interpreted, is the Christ. So chrism and Christ share a root. To be anointed with it is to be marked as belonging to the anointed one. The gospel at this Mass is Jesus in the synagogue at Nazareth, reading from Isaiah: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me. Wherefore he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor." Then the priests stand and renew the promises they made at ordination. The oils go home to every parish, oil for the whole year.
screen: `CHRISM MASS IN HOLY WEEK.` · `CATECHUMENS AND THE SICK.` · `CHRISM: OIL AND BALSAM.` · `CHRIST MEANS ANOINTED.` · then, large: `THE SPIRIT OF THE LORD IS UPON ME.`

segments.voice: Catholics are asked to pray for their priests at this Mass, so if you pray, hold yours in mind: your pastor, the priest who baptized you, one who buried someone you loved. If you're not Catholic, think of anyone who cared for you in a hard moment, a chaplain, a nurse, a friend, and picture their hands. Wish them strength for their own hard days.
Holy oils. The oil of catechumens, the oil of the sick and sacred chrism, blessed by the bishop at the Chrism Mass for the whole year. Today's word.
Your line: oil for the whole year. Every baptism and sickbed draws on it. That's plenty for today.

howItsDone: At the Chrism Mass in Holy Week, the bishop blesses the oil of catechumens and the oil of the sick and consecrates the sacred chrism, and the priests of the diocese renew their ordination promises; each parish then receives the oils for the year.

original.note: Greek: an anointing, ointment; from the same root as Christos, the anointed one.

trapdoor: what you thought: the oils are just olive oil from a store.
what it means: three oils blessed by the bishop each Holy Week for every baptism, confirmation, ordination and anointing in the diocese.
what a scholar hears: chrism and Christ share the Greek root chriō, to anoint; the breathing over the chrism is an optional traditional rite.

chat.says: Where does the oil for baptisms and anointing the sick actually come from?
options: The bishop blesses it at the Chrism Mass in Holy Week, and it goes to every parish.
It's shipped from the Vatican, where the pope blesses one batch for the world.
It's oil pressed on the Mount of Olives and sent to churches every Lent.
